title: Qi Wei responds to the controversy of AI anime drama: Instead of being taken by others, it's better to take the initiative
excerpt: Since the second half of this year, several well-known actors have authorized their faces for AI, sparking heated online discussions. In August this year, actor
content_html:
Since the second half of this year, several well-known actors have authorized their faces for AI, sparking heated online discussions. In August this year, actor and singer Qi Wei announced the trailer of the AI animated drama "Endless Summer," in which the female lead character "Han Qingxia" has the same face as her. Qi Wei said that this character was created by her legally authorized digital avatar.

Netizens summarized this as Qi Wei "selling her face," and this move of embracing AI has also caused a lot of controversy. Recently, Qi Wei candidly stated in an interview with the media that she would rather "take the initiative" than "have her face taken by others."

"No need to act high and mighty," but not considering whether "Endless Summer" can make money yet

In response to the claim that actors take such authorization because they are short on money, Qi Wei replied: It's not true that projects are completely not considered for returns. I have no need to act high and mighty. She believes that a good market should have positive feedback and commercial income, but the field of using AI for content creation is too new, so new that even the rules haven't been established yet. Therefore, she hasn't considered yet whether "Endless Summer" can make money.

She hopes that this act of using AI to generate her image can give the market more confidence. She gave an example that many AIGC creators are very excellent, but most of their creations have not been commercialized yet, which has not dampened their enthusiasm. There are many competition short films both at home and abroad, as well as works from self-taught big names on social media, which are all very impressive. Whether these creators use AI to save money or make money, in her view, they are currently creating for love. In response to the question of whether actors' authorization is due to lack of money, her answer is: Even if you authorize it, it doesn't mean you can make money.

Qi Wei is not the first actor to open up AI authorization. Previously, Hong Kong stars Wu Qihua and Wang Zuxian had already authorized their AI images.
